notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 10 introduces Michael in heavenly conflict; Daniel 12 shows Him standing for His people at the end. Daniel 7 and Revelation 20 connect deliverance with the opened books.

symbols.meaning: Christ rises as heavenly Commander, Judge, and Defender when His mediatorial work is finished.
The judgment record of those who belong to God and are delivered when Michael stands.
The final crisis after probation closes, answered by Christ's deliverance.

wordNotes.explanation: Michael stands up, the great Prince who stands for the children of Daniel's people.
Every one found written in the book is delivered.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12:2 points to resurrection hope and accountability, while Revelation and the Gospels show a special end-time resurrection around Christ's appearing.

symbols.meaning: An end-time resurrection connected with final deliverance and Christ's appearing.

wordNotes.explanation: Death is described as sleep in the dust, and the awakening has two outcomes: everlasting life or shame and everlasting contempt.
The God who remembers names, tears, prayers, and graves will wake His people to everlasting life.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The wise shine because prophetic understanding becomes righteous living and witness.

symbols.meaning: Those who understand the opened prophecy and turn others to righteousness.
Enduring glory for faithful witnesses who lead others to God.

wordNotes.explanation: The wise shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness shine like the stars for ever and ever.
The wise shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness shine like the stars for ever and ever.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel seals the book until the time of the end; Revelation 10 shows the corresponding little book open and recommissions God's people to prophesy.

symbols.meaning: The time-of-the-end portion of Daniel, especially the 2300-day sanctuary prophecy, closed until its appointed time.
Revelation 10's picture of Daniel's sealed prophetic message opened in the time of the end.
Growing understanding of Daniel's opened prophecy after the time of the end begins.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel is told to shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end.
Daniel 8:26 had already said the vision of the evenings and mornings was shut up because it belonged to many days.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12 continues the river setting and heavenly atmosphere introduced in Daniel 10.

symbols.meaning: The final vision returns to the river setting of Daniel 10, showing that chapters 10-12 form one unit.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel sees two others standing, one on each side of the river.
The scene returns to the river setting of the final vision, reminding the reader that Daniel 10, 11, and 12 belong together.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The question in Daniel 12 echoes Daniel 8 and is answered in language that Revelation 10 later develops.

symbols.meaning: The majestic heavenly figure connected with priestly purity, Christ's authority, and the final oath.

wordNotes.explanation: One asks the man clothed in linen, who is above the waters of the river, how long it will be to the end of these wonders.
The one who answers is above the waters, not trapped within the flow of earthly history.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12 gives the oath over the 1260 years; Revelation 10 echoes the oath when the little book is open and prophetic time reaches its limit.

symbols.meaning: The 1260-year period of papal supremacy, reaching from A.D. 538 to A.D. 1798.
A solemn divine oath that links Daniel 12 with Revelation 10's open-book scene.

wordNotes.explanation: The man clothed in linen lifts both hands to heaven and swears by Him who lives forever.
The answer is a time, times, and a half, and when the scattering of the holy people is finished, these things move toward completion.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel's limited understanding in chapter 8 is addressed by the final explanation in chapters 10-12.

symbols.meaning: The prophet's humble desire to understand the outcome of the long conflict.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel hears but does not understand, so he asks, 'O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things?' The prophet is honest about the limits of his understanding.
He does not pretend to master what God has not yet opened.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The closed book in Daniel becomes the opened little book of Revelation 10.

symbols.meaning: The preserved prophetic message opened when the time of the end arrives.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel is told to go his way because the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
Daniel received the prophecy; the time-of-the-end generation would understand and proclaim it.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel's wise are more than informed; they are purified and prepared by the truth they understand.

symbols.meaning: Moral and prophetic understanding given to those who receive the opened message.

wordNotes.explanation: Many are purified, made white, and tried; the wicked do wickedly; none of the wicked understand, but the wise understand.
The wise understand because they are being purified.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12:11 points back to Daniel 11:31 and gives another timeline reaching the beginning of the time of the end in 1798.

symbols.meaning: A prophetic period from A.D. 508 to A.D. 1798, marking the removal of the daily and the rise of the abomination.

wordNotes.term: daily sacrifice shall be taken away
wordNotes.explanation: From the taking away of the daily and the setting up of the abomination, there are 1290 prophetic days.

wordNotes.term: thousand two hundred and ninety days
wordNotes.explanation: The two actions belong together: pagan resistance is removed so the desolating religious-political system can be established.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The 1335 days point to the blessing of living in the era when Daniel's sealed prophecy was opened and proclaimed.

symbols.meaning: A prophetic period from A.D. 508 to the 1843/1844 prophetic awakening, blessing those who waited for the opened message.
The opened message of Daniel received with joy, followed by disappointment and renewed mission.

wordNotes.term: thousand three hundred and five and thirty days
wordNotes.explanation: A blessing is pronounced on the one who waits and comes to the 1335 days.
The blessed waiters are students, witnesses, worshipers, and people being purified.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The book closes by giving Daniel both rest in death and hope of standing in his appointed inheritance.

symbols.meaning: Death described with resurrection hope rather than defeat.
Daniel's appointed inheritance and the way his prophecy stands in its place after the book is opened.

wordNotes.explanation: The book closes with a personal word to Daniel: go thy way till the end, for thou shalt rest and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
The book closes with a personal word to Daniel: go thy way till the end, for thou shalt rest and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
